The '''2020 Copa Sudamericana first stage''' was played from 4 to 27 February 2020.<ref name="calendar">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/calendario_2020_aprobado_consejo_13_06_2019.pdf|title=CALENDÁRIO 2020: CONMEBOL Libertadores - CONMEBOL Sudamericana - RECOPA|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref> A total of 44 teams competed in the first stage to decide 22 of the 32 places in the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana second stage|second stage]] of the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/docs2020/Manual-de-Clubes-Sudamericana-2020-es.pdf|title=Manual de Clubes / Reglamento CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2020|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|language=es}}</ref>

==Draw==
<section begin=Draw />
The draw for the first stage was held on 17 December 2019, 20:30 [[Time in Paraguay|PYST]] ([[UTC−03:00|UTC−3]]), at the CONMEBOL Convention Centre in [[Luque]], [[Paraguay]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/se-sortean-los-cruces-y-grupos-de-la-libertadores-y-sudamericana-2020|title=Se sortean los cruces y grupos de la Libertadores y Sudamericana 2020|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=16 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/pautas-del-sorteo-conmebol-sudamericana-2020|title=Pautas del Sorteo CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2020|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=9 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/los-cruces-de-la-conmebol-sudamericana-0|title=Los cruces de la CONMEBOL Sudamericana|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=17 December 2019}}</ref> For the first stage, the teams were divided into two pots according to their geographical zones:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/dcc_282_2019_-_pauta_del_sorteo_cla_cs_2020_con_bolilleros.pdf|title=CONMEBOL LIBERTADORES 2020 SISTEMA DE SORTEO – Fase Preliminar y Fase de Grupos & CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2020 SISTEMA DE SORTEO – Primera Fase|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref>
*'''Pot A (South Zone):''' 22 teams from Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay
*'''Pot B (North Zone):''' 22 teams from Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela

The 44 teams were drawn into 22 ties (E1–E22) between a team from Pot A and a team from Pot B, with the teams from Pot B hosting the second leg in odd-numbered ties, and the teams from Pot A hosting the second leg in even-numbered ties. This distribution ensured that teams from the same association could not be drawn into the same tie.<section end=Draw />

==Format==
<section begin=Format />
In the first stage, each tie was played on a home-and-away [[two-legged tie|two-legged]] basis. If tied on aggregate, the [[away goals rule]] was used. If still tied, [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] was not played, and a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] was used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 2.4.2).<ref name="regulations"/>

The 22 winners of the first stage advanced to the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana second stage|second stage]] to join the 10 teams transferred from the [[2020 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] (two [[2020 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Copa Sudamericana qualification|best teams]] eliminated in the [[2020 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Third stage|third stage]] of [[2020 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages|qualifying]] and eight third-placed teams in the [[2020 Copa Libertadores group stage|group stage]]).<section end=Format />

==Matches==
The first legs were played on 4–6 and 11–13 February, and the second legs were played on 18–20 and 25–27 February 2020.<ref name="fixture">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/fixture-primera-fase-conmebol-sudamericana-2020|title=Fixture – Primera Fase CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2020|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=18 December 2019|language=es}}</ref><ref name="fixture_pdf">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/fixture_conmebol_sudamericana_22_01_2020.pdf|title=PROGRAMA DE PARTIDOS|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=22 January 2020|language=es}}</ref>
